5|layout: "docs" 6| 7|menu: 8| docs: 9| weight: 20 10|--- 11| 12| 13|# Libraries 14| 15|This chapter will tell you how to make your library installable through Poetry. 16| 17| 18|## Versioning 19| 20|Poetry requires [PEP 440](https://peps.python.org/pep-0440)-compliant versions for all projects. 21| 22|While Poetry does not enforce any release convention, it used to encourage the use of 23|[semantic versioning](https://semver.org/) within the scope of 24|[PEP 440](https://peps.python.org/pep-0440/#semantic-versioning) and supports 25|[version constraints]({{< relref "dependency-specification/#caret-requirements" >}}) 26|that are especially suitable for semver. 27| 28|{{% note %}} 29| 30|As an example, `1.0.0-hotfix.1` is not compatible with [PEP 440](https://peps.python.org/pep-0440). You can instead 31|choose to use `1.0.0-post1` or `1.0.0.post1`. 32| 33|{{% /note %}} 34| 35|## Lock file 36| 37|For your library, you may commit the `poetry.lock` file if you want to. 38|This can help your team to always test against the same dependency versions. 39|However, this lock file will not have any effect on other projects that depend on it. 40|It only has an effect on the main project. 41| 42|If you do not want to commit the lock file and you are using git, add it to the `.gitignore`. 43| 44|## Packaging 45| 46|Before you can actually publish your library, you will need to package it. 47| 48|You need to define a build-system according to [PEP 517](https://peps.python.org/pep-0517/) in the `pyproject.toml` file: 49| 50|```toml 51|[build-system] 52|requires = ["poetry-core>=2.0.0,<3.0.0"] 53|build-backend = "poetry.core.masonry.api" 54|``` 55| 56|Then you can package your library by running: 57| 58|```bash 59|poetry build 60|``` 61| 62|This command will package your library in two different formats: `sdist` which is 63|the source format, and `wheel` which is a `compiled` package. 64| 65|Poetry will automatically include some license-related files when building a package - 66|in the `.dist-info/licenses` directory when building a `wheel`, 67|and in the root folder when building an `sdist`: 68|- `LICENSE*` 69|- `LICENCE*` 70|- `COPYING*` 71|- `AUTHORS*` 72|- `NOTICE*` 73|- `LICENSES/**/*` 74| 75|You can override this behavior by specifying 76|[`license-files`]({{< relref "pyproject/#license-files" >}}) 77|in the `pyproject.toml` file. 78| 79|### Alternative build backends 80| 81|If you want to use a different build backend, you can specify it in the `pyproject.toml` file: 82| 83|```toml 84|[build-system] 85|requires = ["maturin>=0.8.1,<0.9"] 86|build-backend = "maturin" 87|``` 88| 89|The `poetry build` command will then use the specified build backend to build your package in 90|an isolated environment. Ensure you have specified any additional settings according to the 91|documentation of the build backend you are using. 92| 93| 94|Once building is done, you are ready to publish your library. 95| 96|## Publishing to PyPI 97| 98|Alright, so now you can publish packages. 99| 100|Poetry will publish to [PyPI](https://pypi.org) by default. Anything that is published to PyPI 101|is available automatically through Poetry. Since [pendulum](https://pypi.org/project/pendulum/) 102|is on PyPI we can depend on it without having to specify any additional repositories. 103| 104|If we wanted to share `poetry-demo` with the Python community, we would publish on PyPI as well. 105|Doing so is really easy. 106| 107|```bash 108|poetry publish 109|``` 110| 111|This will package and publish the library to PyPI, on the condition that you are a registered user 112|and you have [configured your credentials]({{< relref "repositories#configuring-credentials" >}}) properly. 113| 114|{{% note %}} 115|The `publish` command does not execute `build` by default. 116| 117|If you want to build and publish your packages together, 118|just pass the `--build` option. 119|{{% /note %}} 120| 121|Once this is done, your library will be available to anyone. 122| 123| 124|## Publishing to a private repository 125| 126|Sometimes, you may want to keep your library private but also be accessible to your team. 127| 128|In this case, you will need to use a private repository. 129| 130|In order to publish to a private repository, you will need to add it to your 131|global list of repositories. See [Adding a repository]({{< relref "repositories#adding-a-repository" >}}) 132|for more information. 133| 134|Once this is done, you can publish your package to the repository like so: 135| 136|```bash 137|poetry publish -r my-repository 138|``` --- END FILE: docs/libraries.md --- --- FILE: src/poetry/console/commands/add.py --- 1|from __future__ import annotations 2| 3|import contextlib 4| 5|from typing import TYPE_CHECKING 6|from typing import Any 7|from typing import ClassVar 8|from typing import Literal 9| 10|from cleo.helpers import argument 11|from cleo.helpers import option 12|from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name 13|from poetry.core.packages.dependency import Dependency 14|from poetry.core.packages.dependency_group import MAIN_GROUP 15| 16|from poetry.console.commands.init import InitCommand 17|from poetry.console.commands.installer_command import InstallerCommand 18| 19| 20|if TYPE_CHECKING: 21| from collections.abc import Collection 22| 23| from cleo.io.inputs.argument import Argument 24| from cleo.io.inputs.option import Option 25| from packaging.utils import NormalizedName 26| 27| 28|class AddCommand(InstallerCommand, InitCommand): 29| name = "add" 30| description = "Adds a new dependency to pyproject.toml and installs it." 31| 32| arguments: ClassVar[list[Argument]] = [ 33| argument("name", "The packages to add.", multiple=True) 34| ] 35| options: ClassVar[list[Option]] = [ 36| option( 37| "group", 38| "-G", 39| "The group to add the dependency to.", 40| flag=False, 41| default=MAIN_GROUP, 42| ), 43| option( 44| "dev", 45| "D", 46| "Add as a development dependency.
